question:
A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of episodic bleeding from the nose and gums and one episode of blood in her urine. She was treated with chloramphenicol 1 month ago for Rickettsia rickettsii infection. Her pulse is 130/min, respirations are 22/min, and blood pressure is 105/70 mm Hg. Examination shows mucosal pallor, scattered petechiae, and ecchymoses on the extremities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 6.3 g/dL
Hematocrit 26%
Leukocyte count 900/mm3 (30% neutrophils)
Platelet count 50,000/mm3
The physician recommends a blood transfusion and informs her of the risks and benefits. Which of the following red blood cell preparations will most significantly reduce the risk of transfusion-related cytomegalovirus infection?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Low platelet count -> Increased risk of bleeding -> Episodic bleeding from nose and gums -> Blood in urine -> Suspected thrombocytopenia -> 80% CHAIN: Treatment with chloramphenicol for Rickettsia rickettsii infection -> Possible bone marrow suppression -> Low blood cell counts -> Anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia -> 70% CHAIN: Low platelet count and leukocyte count -> Increased risk of infection -> Susceptibility to transfusion-related cytomegalovirus infection -> 60% CHAIN: Blood transfusion recommended -> Risk of transfusion-related cytomegalovirus infection -> Consideration of red blood cell preparation methods -> 50% CHAIN: Red blood cell preparation methods -> Leukoreduction -> Most significant reduction in transfusion-related cytomegalovirus infection risk -> 80%
analysis: Given the patient's low platelet count and the need for a blood transfusion, the most appropriate red blood cell preparation to reduce the risk of transfusion-related cytomegalovirus infection would be leukoreduction. Leukoreduction involves removing white blood cells from the blood product, which can help decrease the risk of transmitting cytomegalovirus.
